storage.name: Account
docs: The full account information for a particular account ID.

storage.name: ExtrinsicCount
docs: Total extrinsics count for the current block.

storage.name: InherentsApplied
docs: Whether all inherents have been applied.

storage.name: BlockWeight
docs: The current weight for the block.

storage.name: BlockSize
docs: Total size (in bytes) of the current block.
Tracks the size of the header and all extrinsics.

storage.name: BlockHash
docs: Map of block numbers to block hashes.

storage.name: ExtrinsicData
docs: Extrinsics data for the current block (maps an extrinsic's index to its data).

storage.name: Number
docs: The current block number being processed. Set by `execute_block`.

storage.name: ParentHash
docs: Hash of the previous block.

storage.name: Digest
docs: Digest of the current block, also part of the block header.

storage.name: Events
docs: Events deposited for the current block.
NOTE: The item is unbound and should therefore never be read on chain.
It could otherwise inflate the PoV size of a block.
Events have a large in-memory size. Box the events to not go out-of-memory
just in case someone still reads them from within the runtime.

storage.name: EventCount
docs: The number of events in the `Events<T>` list.

storage.name: EventTopics
docs: Mapping between a topic (represented by T::Hash) and a vector of indexes
of events in the `<Events<T>>` list.
All topic vectors have deterministic storage locations depending on the topic. This
allows light-clients to leverage the changes trie storage tracking mechanism and
in case of changes fetch the list of events of interest.
The value has the type `(BlockNumberFor<T>, EventIndex)` because if we used only just
the `EventIndex` then in case if the topic has the same contents on the next block
no notification will be triggered thus the event might be lost.

storage.name: LastRuntimeUpgrade
docs: Stores the `spec_version` and `spec_name` of when the last runtime upgrade happened.

storage.name: BlocksTillUpgrade
docs: Number of blocks till the pending code upgrade is applied.

storage.name: UpgradedToU32RefCount
docs: True if we have upgraded so that `type RefCount` is `u32`. False (default) if not.

storage.name: UpgradedToTripleRefCount
docs: True if we have upgraded so that AccountInfo contains three types of `RefCount`. False
(default) if not.

storage.name: ExecutionPhase
docs: The execution phase of the block.

storage.name: AuthorizedUpgrade
docs: `Some` if a code upgrade has been authorized.

storage.name: ExtrinsicWeightReclaimed
docs: The weight reclaimed for the extrinsic.
This information is available until the end of the extrinsic execution.
More precisely this information is removed in `note_applied_extrinsic`.
Logic doing some post dispatch weight reduction must update this storage to avoid duplicate
reduction.

storage.name: EpochIndex
docs: Current epoch index.

storage.name: Authorities
docs: Current epoch authorities.

storage.name: GenesisSlot
docs: The slot at which the first epoch actually started. This is 0
until the first block of the chain.

storage.name: CurrentSlot
docs: Current slot number.

storage.name: Randomness
docs: The epoch randomness for the *current* epoch.
# Security
This MUST NOT be used for gambling, as it can be influenced by a
malicious validator in the short term. It MAY be used in many
cryptographic protocols, however, so long as one remembers that this
(like everything else on-chain) it is public. For example, it can be
used where a number is needed that cannot have been chosen by an
adversary, for purposes such as public-coin zero-knowledge proofs.

storage.name: PendingEpochConfigChange
docs: Pending epoch configuration change that will be applied when the next epoch is enacted.

storage.name: NextRandomness
docs: Next epoch randomness.

storage.name: NextAuthorities
docs: Next epoch authorities.

storage.name: SegmentIndex
docs: Randomness under construction.
We make a trade-off between storage accesses and list length.
We store the under-construction randomness in segments of up to
`UNDER_CONSTRUCTION_SEGMENT_LENGTH`.
Once a segment reaches this length, we begin the next one.
We reset all segments and return to `0` at the beginning of every
epoch.

storage.name: UnderConstruction
docs: TWOX-NOTE: `SegmentIndex` is an increasing integer, so this is okay.

storage.name: Initialized
docs: Temporary value (cleared at block finalization) which is `Some`
if per-block initialization has already been called for current block.

storage.name: AuthorVrfRandomness
docs: This field should always be populated during block processing unless
secondary plain slots are enabled (which don't contain a VRF output).
It is set in `on_finalize`, before it will contain the value from the last block.

storage.name: EpochStart
docs: The block numbers when the last and current epoch have started, respectively `N-1` and
NOTE: We track this is in order to annotate the block number when a given pool of
entropy was fixed (i.e. it was known to chain observers). Since epochs are defined in
slots, which may be skipped, the block numbers may not line up with the slot numbers.

storage.name: Lateness
docs: How late the current block is compared to its parent.
This entry is populated as part of block execution and is cleaned up
on block finalization. Querying this storage entry outside of block
execution context should always yield zero.

storage.name: EpochConfig
docs: The configuration for the current epoch. Should never be `None` as it is initialized in
genesis.

storage.name: NextEpochConfig
docs: The configuration for the next epoch, `None` if the config will not change
(you can fallback to `EpochConfig` instead in that case).

storage.name: SkippedEpochs
docs: A list of the last 100 skipped epochs and the corresponding session index
when the epoch was skipped.
This is only used for validating equivocation proofs. An equivocation proof
must contains a key-ownership proof for a given session, therefore we need a
way to tie together sessions and epoch indices, i.e. we need to validate that
a validator was the owner of a given key on a given session, and what the
active epoch index was during that session.

storage.name: Now
docs: The current time for the current block.

storage.name: DidUpdate
docs: Whether the timestamp has been updated in this block.
This value is updated to `true` upon successful submission of a timestamp by a node.
It is then checked at the end of each block execution in the `on_finalize` hook.

storage.name: Author
docs: Author of current block.

storage.name: Accounts
docs: The lookup from index to account.

storage.name: TotalIssuance
docs: The total units issued in the system.

storage.name: InactiveIssuance
docs: The total units of outstanding deactivated balance in the system.

storage.name: Account
docs: The Balances pallet example of storing the balance of an account.
# Example
```nocompile
impl pallet_balances::Config for Runtime {
type AccountStore = StorageMapShim<Self::Account<Runtime>, frame_system::Provider<Runtime>, AccountId, Self::AccountData<Balance>>
You can also store the balance of an account in the `System` pallet.
# Example
```nocompile
impl pallet_balances::Config for Runtime {
type AccountStore = System
But this comes with tradeoffs, storing account balances in the system pallet stores
`frame_system` data alongside the account data contrary to storing account balances in the
`Balances` pallet, which uses a `StorageMap` to store balances data only.
NOTE: This is only used in the case that this pallet is used to store balances.

storage.name: Locks
docs: Any liquidity locks on some account balances.
NOTE: Should only be accessed when setting, changing and freeing a lock.
Use of locks is deprecated in favour of freezes. See `https://github.com/paritytech/substrate/pull/12951/`

storage.name: Reserves
docs: Named reserves on some account balances.
Use of reserves is deprecated in favour of holds. See `https://github.com/paritytech/substrate/pull/12951/`

storage.name: Holds
docs: Holds on account balances.

storage.name: Freezes
docs: Freeze locks on account balances.

storage.name: TxPaymentCredit
docs: The `OnChargeTransaction` stores the withdrawn tx fee here.
Use `withdraw_txfee` and `remaining_txfee` to access from outside the crate.

storage.name: Round
docs: Internal counter for the number of rounds.
This is useful for de-duplication of transactions submitted to the pool, and general
diagnostics of the pallet.
This is merely incremented once per every time that an upstream `elect` is called.

storage.name: CurrentPhase
docs: Current phase.

storage.name: QueuedSolution
docs: Current best solution, signed or unsigned, queued to be returned upon `elect`.
Always sorted by score.

storage.name: Snapshot
docs: Snapshot data of the round.
This is created at the beginning of the signed phase and cleared upon calling `elect`.
Note: This storage type must only be mutated through [`SnapshotWrapper`].

storage.name: DesiredTargets
docs: Desired number of targets to elect for this round.
Only exists when [`Snapshot`] is present.
Note: This storage type must only be mutated through [`SnapshotWrapper`].

storage.name: SnapshotMetadata
docs: The metadata of the [`RoundSnapshot`]
Only exists when [`Snapshot`] is present.
Note: This storage type must only be mutated through [`SnapshotWrapper`].

storage.name: SignedSubmissionNextIndex
docs: The next index to be assigned to an incoming signed submission.
Every accepted submission is assigned a unique index; that index is bound to that particular
submission for the duration of the election. On election finalization, the next index is
reset to 0.
We can't just use `SignedSubmissionIndices.len()`, because that's a bounded set; past its
capacity, it will simply saturate. We can't just iterate over `SignedSubmissionsMap`,
because iteration is slow. Instead, we store the value here.

storage.name: SignedSubmissionIndices
docs: A sorted, bounded vector of `(score, block_number, index)`, where each `index` points to a
value in `SignedSubmissions`.
We never need to process more than a single signed submission at a time. Signed submissions
can be quite large, so we're willing to pay the cost of multiple database accesses to access
them one at a time instead of reading and decoding all of them at once.

storage.name: SignedSubmissionsMap
docs: Unchecked, signed solutions.
Together with `SubmissionIndices`, this stores a bounded set of `SignedSubmissions` while
allowing us to keep only a single one in memory at a time.
Twox note: the key of the map is an auto-incrementing index which users cannot inspect or
affect; we shouldn't need a cryptographically secure hasher.

storage.name: MinimumUntrustedScore
docs: The minimum score that each 'untrusted' solution must attain in order to be considered
feasible.
Can be set via `set_minimum_untrusted_score`.

storage.name: ValidatorCount
docs: The ideal number of active validators.

storage.name: MinimumValidatorCount
docs: Minimum number of staking participants before emergency conditions are imposed.

storage.name: Invulnerables
docs: Any validators that may never be slashed or forcibly kicked. It's a Vec since they're
easy to initialize and the performance hit is minimal (we expect no more than four
invulnerables) and restricted to testnets.

storage.name: Bonded
docs: Map from all locked "stash" accounts to the controller account.
TWOX-NOTE: SAFE since `AccountId` is a secure hash.

storage.name: MinNominatorBond
docs: The minimum active bond to become and maintain the role of a nominator.

storage.name: MinValidatorBond
docs: The minimum active bond to become and maintain the role of a validator.

storage.name: MinimumActiveStake
docs: The minimum active nominator stake of the last successful election.

storage.name: MinCommission
docs: The minimum amount of commission that validators can set.
If set to `0`, no limit exists.

storage.name: Ledger
docs: Map from all (unlocked) "controller" accounts to the info regarding the staking.
Note: All the reads and mutations to this storage *MUST* be done through the methods exposed
by [`StakingLedger`] to ensure data and lock consistency.

storage.name: Payee
docs: Where the reward payment should be made. Keyed by stash.
TWOX-NOTE: SAFE since `AccountId` is a secure hash.

storage.name: Validators
docs: The map from (wannabe) validator stash key to the preferences of that validator.
TWOX-NOTE: SAFE since `AccountId` is a secure hash.

storage.name: CounterForValidators
docs: Counter for the related counted storage map

storage.name: MaxValidatorsCount
docs: The maximum validator count before we stop allowing new validators to join.
When this value is not set, no limits are enforced.

storage.name: Nominators
docs: The map from nominator stash key to their nomination preferences, namely the validators that
they wish to support.
Note that the keys of this storage map might become non-decodable in case the
account's [`NominationsQuota::MaxNominations`] configuration is decreased.
In this rare case, these nominators
are still existent in storage, their key is correct and retrievable (i.e. `contains_key`
indicates that they exist), but their value cannot be decoded. Therefore, the non-decodable
nominators will effectively not-exist, until they re-submit their preferences such that it
is within the bounds of the newly set `Config::MaxNominations`.
This implies that `::iter_keys().count()` and `::iter().count()` might return different
values for this map. Moreover, the main `::count()` is aligned with the former, namely the
number of keys that exist.
Lastly, if any of the nominators become non-decodable, they can be chilled immediately via
[`Call::chill_other`] dispatchable by anyone.
TWOX-NOTE: SAFE since `AccountId` is a secure hash.

storage.name: CounterForNominators
docs: Counter for the related counted storage map

storage.name: VirtualStakers
docs: Stakers whose funds are managed by other pallets.
This pallet does not apply any locks on them, therefore they are only virtually bonded. They
are expected to be keyless accounts and hence should not be allowed to mutate their ledger
directly via this pallet. Instead, these accounts are managed by other pallets and accessed
via low level apis. We keep track of them to do minimal integrity checks.

storage.name: CounterForVirtualStakers
docs: Counter for the related counted storage map

storage.name: MaxNominatorsCount
docs: The maximum nominator count before we stop allowing new validators to join.
When this value is not set, no limits are enforced.

storage.name: CurrentEra
docs: The current era index.
This is the latest planned era, depending on how the Session pallet queues the validator
set, it might be active or not.

storage.name: ActiveEra
docs: The active era information, it holds index and start.
The active era is the era being currently rewarded. Validator set of this era must be
equal to [`SessionInterface::validators`].

storage.name: ErasStartSessionIndex
docs: The session index at which the era start for the last [`Config::HistoryDepth`] eras.
Note: This tracks the starting session (i.e. session index when era start being active)
for the eras in `[CurrentEra - HISTORY_DEPTH, CurrentEra]`.

storage.name: ErasStakers
docs: Exposure of validator at era.
This is keyed first by the era index to allow bulk deletion and then the stash account.
Is it removed after [`Config::HistoryDepth`] eras.
If stakers hasn't been set or has been removed then empty exposure is returned.
Note: Deprecated since v14. Use `EraInfo` instead to work with exposures.

storage.name: ErasStakersOverview
docs: Summary of validator exposure at a given era.
This contains the total stake in support of the validator and their own stake. In addition,
it can also be used to get the number of nominators backing this validator and the number of
exposure pages they are divided into. The page count is useful to determine the number of
pages of rewards that needs to be claimed.
This is keyed first by the era index to allow bulk deletion and then the stash account.
Should only be accessed through `EraInfo`.
Is it removed after [`Config::HistoryDepth`] eras.
If stakers hasn't been set or has been removed then empty overview is returned.

storage.name: ErasStakersClipped
docs: Clipped Exposure of validator at era.
Note: This is deprecated, should be used as read-only and will be removed in the future.
New `Exposure`s are stored in a paged manner in `ErasStakersPaged` instead.
This is similar to [`ErasStakers`] but number of nominators exposed is reduced to the
`T::MaxExposurePageSize` biggest stakers.
(Note: the field `total` and `own` of the exposure remains unchanged).
This is used to limit the i/o cost for the nominator payout.
This is keyed fist by the era index to allow bulk deletion and then the stash account.
It is removed after [`Config::HistoryDepth`] eras.
If stakers hasn't been set or has been removed then empty exposure is returned.
Note: Deprecated since v14. Use `EraInfo` instead to work with exposures.

storage.name: ErasStakersPaged
docs: Paginated exposure of a validator at given era.
This is keyed first by the era index to allow bulk deletion, then stash account and finally
the page. Should only be accessed through `EraInfo`.
This is cleared after [`Config::HistoryDepth`] eras.

storage.name: ClaimedRewards
docs: History of claimed paged rewards by era and validator.
This is keyed by era and validator stash which maps to the set of page indexes which have
been claimed.
It is removed after [`Config::HistoryDepth`] eras.

storage.name: ErasValidatorPrefs
docs: Similar to `ErasStakers`, this holds the preferences of validators.
This is keyed first by the era index to allow bulk deletion and then the stash account.
Is it removed after [`Config::HistoryDepth`] eras.

storage.name: ErasValidatorReward
docs: The total validator era payout for the last [`Config::HistoryDepth`] eras.
Eras that haven't finished yet or has been removed doesn't have reward.

storage.name: ErasRewardPoints
docs: Rewards for the last [`Config::HistoryDepth`] eras.
If reward hasn't been set or has been removed then 0 reward is returned.

storage.name: ErasTotalStake
docs: The total amount staked for the last [`Config::HistoryDepth`] eras.
If total hasn't been set or has been removed then 0 stake is returned.

storage.name: ForceEra
docs: Mode of era forcing.

storage.name: MaxStakedRewards
docs: Maximum staked rewards, i.e. the percentage of the era inflation that
is used for stake rewards.
See [Era payout](./index.html#era-payout).

storage.name: SlashRewardFraction
docs: The percentage of the slash that is distributed to reporters.
The rest of the slashed value is handled by the `Slash`.

storage.name: CanceledSlashPayout
docs: The amount of currency given to reporters of a slash event which was
canceled by extraordinary circumstances (e.g. governance).

storage.name: UnappliedSlashes
docs: All unapplied slashes that are queued for later.

storage.name: BondedEras
docs: A mapping from still-bonded eras to the first session index of that era.
Must contains information for eras for the range:
`[active_era - bounding_duration; active_era]`

storage.name: ValidatorSlashInEra
docs: All slashing events on validators, mapped by era to the highest slash proportion
and slash value of the era.

storage.name: NominatorSlashInEra
docs: All slashing events on nominators, mapped by era to the highest slash value of the era.

storage.name: SlashingSpans
docs: Slashing spans for stash accounts.

storage.name: SpanSlash
docs: Records information about the maximum slash of a stash within a slashing span,
as well as how much reward has been paid out.

storage.name: CurrentPlannedSession
docs: The last planned session scheduled by the session pallet.
This is basically in sync with the call to [`pallet_session::SessionManager::new_session`].

storage.name: ChillThreshold
docs: The threshold for when users can start calling `chill_other` for other validators /
nominators. The threshold is compared to the actual number of validators / nominators
(`CountFor*`) in the system compared to the configured max (`Max*Count`).

storage.name: Validators
docs: The current set of validators.

storage.name: CurrentIndex
docs: Current index of the session.

storage.name: QueuedChanged
docs: True if the underlying economic identities or weighting behind the validators
has changed in the queued validator set.

storage.name: QueuedKeys
docs: The queued keys for the next session. When the next session begins, these keys
will be used to determine the validator's session keys.

storage.name: DisabledValidators
docs: Indices of disabled validators.
The vec is always kept sorted so that we can find whether a given validator is
disabled using binary search. It gets cleared when `on_session_ending` returns
a new set of identities.

storage.name: NextKeys
docs: The next session keys for a validator.

storage.name: KeyOwner
docs: The owner of a key. The key is the `KeyTypeId` + the encoded key.

storage.name: ExternallySetKeys
docs: Accounts whose keys were set via `SessionInterface` (external path) without
incrementing the consumer reference or placing a key deposit. `do_purge_keys`
only decrements consumers for accounts that were registered through the local
session pallet.

storage.name: Proposals
docs: The hashes of the active proposals.

storage.name: ProposalOf
docs: Actual proposal for a given hash, if it's current.

storage.name: CostOf
docs: Consideration cost created for publishing and storing a proposal.
Determined by [Config::Consideration] and may be not present for certain proposals (e.g. if
the proposal count at the time of creation was below threshold N).

storage.name: Voting
docs: Votes on a given proposal, if it is ongoing.

storage.name: ProposalCount
docs: Proposals so far.

storage.name: Members
docs: The current members of the collective. This is stored sorted (just by value).

storage.name: Prime
docs: The prime member that helps determine the default vote behavior in case of abstentions.

storage.name: Members
docs: The current membership, stored as an ordered Vec.

storage.name: Prime
docs: The current prime member, if one exists.

storage.name: State
docs: State of the current authority set.

storage.name: PendingChange
docs: Pending change: (signaled at, scheduled change).

storage.name: NextForced
docs: next block number where we can force a change.

storage.name: Stalled
docs: `true` if we are currently stalled.

storage.name: CurrentSetId
docs: The number of changes (both in terms of keys and underlying economic responsibilities)
in the "set" of Grandpa validators from genesis.

storage.name: SetIdSession
docs: A mapping from grandpa set ID to the index of the *most recent* session for which its
members were responsible.
This is only used for validating equivocation proofs. An equivocation proof must
contains a key-ownership proof for a given session, therefore we need a way to tie
together sessions and GRANDPA set ids, i.e. we need to validate that a validator
was the owner of a given key on a given session, and what the active set ID was
during that session.
TWOX-NOTE: `SetId` is not under user control.

storage.name: Authorities
docs: The current list of authorities.

storage.name: ProposalCount
docs: DEPRECATED: associated with `spend_local` call and will be removed in May 2025.
Refer to <https://github.com/paritytech/polkadot-sdk/pull/5961> for migration to `spend`.
Number of proposals that have been made.

storage.name: Proposals
docs: DEPRECATED: associated with `spend_local` call and will be removed in May 2025.
Refer to <https://github.com/paritytech/polkadot-sdk/pull/5961> for migration to `spend`.
Proposals that have been made.

storage.name: Deactivated
docs: The amount which has been reported as inactive to Currency.

storage.name: Approvals
docs: DEPRECATED: associated with `spend_local` call and will be removed in May 2025.
Refer to <https://github.com/paritytech/polkadot-sdk/pull/5961> for migration to `spend`.
Proposal indices that have been approved but not yet awarded.

storage.name: SpendCount
docs: The count of spends that have been made.

storage.name: Spends
docs: Spends that have been approved and being processed.

storage.name: LastSpendPeriod
docs: The blocknumber for the last triggered spend period.

storage.name: ConversionRateToNative
docs: Maps an asset to its fixed point representation in the native balance.
E.g. `native_amount = asset_amount * ConversionRateToNative::<T>::get(asset_kind)`

storage.name: PristineCode
docs: A mapping from a contract's code hash to its code.

storage.name: CodeInfoOf
docs: A mapping from a contract's code hash to its code info.

storage.name: Nonce
docs: This is a **monotonic** counter incremented on contract instantiation.
This is used in order to generate unique trie ids for contracts.
The trie id of a new contract is calculated from hash(account_id, nonce).
The nonce is required because otherwise the following sequence would lead to
a possible collision of storage:
1. Create a new contract.
2. Terminate the contract.
3. Immediately recreate the contract with the same account_id.
This is bad because the contents of a trie are deleted lazily and there might be
storage of the old instantiation still in it when the new contract is created. Please
note that we can't replace the counter by the block number because the sequence above
can happen in the same block. We also can't keep the account counter in memory only
because storage is the only way to communicate across different extrinsics in the
same block.
# Note
Do not use it to determine the number of contracts. It won't be decremented if
a contract is destroyed.

storage.name: ContractInfoOf
docs: The code associated with a given account.
TWOX-NOTE: SAFE since `AccountId` is a secure hash.

storage.name: DeletionQueue
docs: Evicted contracts that await child trie deletion.
Child trie deletion is a heavy operation depending on the amount of storage items
stored in said trie. Therefore this operation is performed lazily in `on_idle`.

storage.name: DeletionQueueCounter
docs: A pair of monotonic counters used to track the latest contract marked for deletion
and the latest deleted contract in queue.

storage.name: MigrationInProgress
docs: A migration can span across multiple blocks. This storage defines a cursor to track the
progress of the migration, enabling us to resume from the last completed position.

storage.name: Key
docs: The `AccountId` of the sudo key.

storage.name: HeartbeatAfter
docs: The block number after which it's ok to send heartbeats in the current
session.
At the beginning of each session we set this to a value that should fall
roughly in the middle of the session duration. The idea is to first wait for
the validators to produce a block in the current session, so that the
heartbeat later on will not be necessary.
This value will only be used as a fallback if we fail to get a proper session
progress estimate from `NextSessionRotation`, as those estimates should be
more accurate then the value we calculate for `HeartbeatAfter`.

storage.name: Keys
docs: The current set of keys that may issue a heartbeat.

storage.name: ReceivedHeartbeats
docs: For each session index, we keep a mapping of `SessionIndex` and `AuthIndex`.

storage.name: AuthoredBlocks
docs: For each session index, we keep a mapping of `ValidatorId<T>` to the
number of blocks authored by the given authority.

storage.name: Keys
docs: Keys of the current authority set.

storage.name: NextKeys
docs: Keys of the next authority set.

storage.name: Reports
docs: The primary structure that holds all offence records keyed by report identifiers.

storage.name: ConcurrentReportsIndex
docs: A vector of reports of the same kind that happened at the same time slot.

storage.name: HistoricalSessions
docs: Mapping from historical session indices to session-data root hash and validator count.

storage.name: StoredRange
docs: The range of historical sessions we store. [first, last)

storage.name: IdentityOf
docs: Information that is pertinent to identify the entity behind an account. First item is the
registration, second is the account's primary username.
TWOX-NOTE: OK ― `AccountId` is a secure hash.

storage.name: UsernameOf
docs: Identifies the primary username of an account.

storage.name: SuperOf
docs: The super-identity of an alternative "sub" identity together with its name, within that
context. If the account is not some other account's sub-identity, then just `None`.

storage.name: SubsOf
docs: Alternative "sub" identities of this account.
The first item is the deposit, the second is a vector of the accounts.
TWOX-NOTE: OK ― `AccountId` is a secure hash.

storage.name: Registrars
docs: The set of registrars. Not expected to get very big as can only be added through a
special origin (likely a council motion).
The index into this can be cast to `RegistrarIndex` to get a valid value.

storage.name: AuthorityOf
docs: A map of the accounts who are authorized to grant usernames.

storage.name: UsernameInfoOf
docs: Reverse lookup from `username` to the `AccountId` that has registered it and the provider of
the username. The `owner` value should be a key in the `UsernameOf` map, but it may not if
the user has cleared their username or it has been removed.
Multiple usernames may map to the same `AccountId`, but `UsernameOf` will only map to one
primary username.

storage.name: PendingUsernames
docs: Usernames that an authority has granted, but that the account controller has not confirmed
that they want it. Used primarily in cases where the `AccountId` cannot provide a signature
because they are a pure proxy, multisig, etc. In order to confirm it, they should call
[accept_username](`Call::accept_username`).
First tuple item is the account and second is the acceptance deadline.

storage.name: UnbindingUsernames

storage.name: FriendGroups

storage.name: Attempt

storage.name: Inheritor

storage.name: Vesting
docs: Information regarding the vesting of a given account.

storage.name: StorageVersion
docs: Storage version of the pallet.
New networks start with latest version, as determined by the genesis build.

storage.name: IncompleteSince

storage.name: Agenda

storage.name: Retries

storage.name: Lookup

For v3 -> v4 the previously unbounded identities are Blake2-256 hashed to form the v4
identities.

storage.name: StatusFor

storage.name: RequestStatusFor
docs: The request status of a given hash.

storage.name: Proxies
docs: The set of account proxies. Maps the account which has delegated to the accounts
which are being delegated to, together with the amount held on deposit.

storage.name: Announcements

storage.name: Multisigs

storage.name: BountyApprovals

storage.name: Reserves

storage.name: NextAssetId

provide an initial value here to apply an auto-increment model to all new asset IDs.
The initial next asset ID can be set using the [`GenesisConfig`] or the
[SetNextAssetId](`migration::next_asset_id::SetNextAssetId`) migration.

docs: Details of an asset.

storage.name: Account
docs: The holdings of a specific account for a specific asset.

storage.name: Approvals
docs: Approved balance transfers. First balance is the amount approved for transfer. Second
is the amount of `T::Currency` reserved for storing this.
First key is the asset ID, second key is the owner and third key is the delegate.

storage.name: NextAssetId

item has no effect.
Only read by [`crate::AutoIncAssetId`]: configure it as [`Config::AssetIdAllocator`] and
provide an initial value here to apply an auto-increment model to all new asset IDs.
The initial next asset ID can be set using the [`GenesisConfig`] or the
[SetNextAssetId](`migration::next_asset_id::SetNextAssetId`) migration.

storage.name: Authorities

storage.name: ValidatorSetId

storage.name: NextAuthorities
docs: Authorities set scheduled to be used with the next session

storage.name: SetIdSession
docs: A mapping from BEEFY set ID to the index of the *most recent* session for which its
members were responsible.
This is only used for validating equivocation proofs. An equivocation proof must
contains a key-ownership proof for a given session, therefore we need a way to tie
together sessions and BEEFY set ids, i.e. we need to validate that a validator
was the owner of a given key on a given session, and what the active set ID was
during that session.
TWOX-NOTE: `ValidatorSetId` is not under user control.

storage.name: GenesisBlock
docs: Block number where BEEFY consensus is enabled/started.
By changing this (through privileged `set_new_genesis()`), BEEFY consensus is effectively
restarted from the newly set block number.

storage.name: RootHash
docs: Latest MMR Root hash.

storage.name: NumberOfLeaves
docs: Current size of the MMR (number of leaves).

storage.name: Nodes
docs: Hashes of the nodes in the MMR.
Note this collection only contains MMR peaks, the inner nodes (and leaves)
are pruned and only stored in the Offchain DB.

storage.name: BeefyAuthorities
docs: Details of current BEEFY authority set.

storage.name: BeefyNextAuthorities
docs: Details of next BEEFY authority set.
This storage entry is used as cache for calls to `update_beefy_next_authority_set`.

storage.name: Lottery
docs: The configuration for the current lottery.

storage.name: Participants
docs: Users who have purchased a ticket. (Lottery Index, Tickets Purchased)

storage.name: TicketsCount
docs: Total number of tickets sold.

storage.name: Tickets
docs: Each ticket's owner.
May have residual storage from previous lotteries. Use `TicketsCount` to see which ones
are actually valid ticket mappings.

storage.name: CallIndices
docs: The calls stored in this pallet to be used in an active lottery if configured
by `Config::ValidateCall`.

storage.name: Class
docs: Details of a collection.

storage.name: OwnershipAcceptance
docs: The collection, if any, of which an account is willing to take ownership.

storage.name: Account
docs: The items held by any given account; set out this way so that items owned by a single
account can be enumerated.

storage.name: ClassAccount
docs: The collections owned by any given account; set out this way so that collections owned by
a single account can be enumerated.

storage.name: Asset
docs: The items in existence and their ownership details.

storage.name: ClassMetadataOf
docs: Metadata of a collection.

storage.name: InstanceMetadataOf
docs: Metadata of an item.

storage.name: Attribute
docs: Attributes of a collection.

storage.name: ItemPriceOf
docs: Price of an asset instance.

storage.name: CollectionMaxSupply
docs: Keeps track of the number of items a collection might have.

storage.name: Collection
docs: Details of a collection.

storage.name: OwnershipAcceptance
docs: The collection, if any, of which an account is willing to take ownership.

storage.name: Account
docs: The items held by any given account; set out this way so that items owned by a single
account can be enumerated.

storage.name: CollectionAccount
docs: The collections owned by any given account; set out this way so that collections owned by
a single account can be enumerated.

storage.name: CollectionRoleOf
docs: The items in existence and their ownership details.
Stores collection roles as per account.

storage.name: Item
docs: The items in existence and their ownership details.

storage.name: CollectionMetadataOf
docs: Metadata of a collection.

storage.name: ItemMetadataOf
docs: Metadata of an item.

storage.name: Attribute
docs: Attributes of a collection.

storage.name: ItemPriceOf
docs: A price of an item.

storage.name: ItemAttributesApprovalsOf
docs: Item attribute approvals.

storage.name: NextCollectionId
docs: Stores the `CollectionId` that is going to be used for the next collection.
This gets incremented whenever a new collection is created.

storage.name: PendingSwapOf
docs: Handles all the pending swaps.

storage.name: CollectionConfigOf
docs: Config of a collection.

storage.name: ItemConfigOf
docs: Config of an item.

storage.name: NftToAsset
docs: Keeps track of the corresponding NFT ID, asset ID and amount minted.

storage.name: Authorizations
docs: Authorizations, keyed by scope.

storage.name: Transactions
docs: Collection of transaction metadata by block number.

storage.name: ByteFee
docs: Storage fee per byte.

storage.name: EntryFee
docs: Storage fee per transaction.

storage.name: RetentionPeriod
docs: Number of blocks for which stored data must be retained.
Data older than `RetentionPeriod` blocks is eligible for removal unless it
has been explicitly renewed. Validators are required to prove possession of
data corresponding to block `N - RetentionPeriod` when producing block `N`.

storage.name: ProofChecked
docs: Was the proof checked in this block?

storage.name: ListNodes
docs: A single node, within some bag.
Nodes store links forward and back within their respective bags.

storage.name: CounterForListNodes
docs: Counter for the related counted storage map

storage.name: ListBags
docs: A bag stored in storage.
Stores a `Bag` struct, which stores head and tail pointers to itself.

storage.name: NextNodeAutoRebagged
docs: Pointer that remembers the next node that will be auto-rebagged.
When `None`, the next scan will start from the list head again.

storage.name: Lock
docs: Lock all updates to this pallet.
If any nodes needs updating, removal or addition due to a temporary lock, the
[`Call::rebag`] can be used.

storage.name: PendingRebag
docs: Accounts that failed to be inserted into the bags-list due to locking.
These accounts will be processed with priority in `on_idle` or via `rebag` extrinsic.
Note: This storage is intentionally unbounded. The following factors make bounding
unnecessary:
1. The storage usage is temporary - accounts are processed and removed in `on_idle`
2. The pallet is only locked during snapshot generation, which is weight-limited
3. Processing happens at multiple accounts per block, clearing even large backlogs quickly
4. An artificial limit could be exhausted by an attacker, preventing legitimate
auto-rebagging from putting accounts in the correct position
We don't store the score here - it's always fetched from `ScoreProvider` when processing,
ensuring we use the most up-to-date score (accounts may have been slashed, rewarded, etc.
while waiting in the queue).

storage.name: CounterForPendingRebag
docs: Counter for the related counted storage map

storage.name: ChildBountyCount
docs: DEPRECATED: Replaced with `ParentTotalChildBounties` storage item keeping dedicated counts
for each parent bounty. Number of total child bounties. Will be removed in May 2025.

storage.name: ParentChildBounties
docs: Number of active child bounties per parent bounty.
Map of parent bounty index to number of child bounties.

storage.name: ParentTotalChildBounties
docs: Number of total child bounties per parent bounty, including completed bounties.

storage.name: ChildBounties
docs: Child bounties that have been added.

storage.name: ChildBountyDescriptionsV1
docs: The description of each child-bounty. Indexed by `(parent_id, child_id)`.
This item replaces the `ChildBountyDescriptions` storage item from the V0 storage version.

storage.name: V0ToV1ChildBountyIds
docs: The mapping of the child bounty ids from storage version `V0` to the new `V1` version.
The `V0` ids based on total child bounty count [`ChildBountyCount`]`. The `V1` version ids
based on the child bounty count per parent bounty [`ParentTotalChildBounties`].
The item intended solely for client convenience and not used in the pallet's core logic.

storage.name: ChildrenCuratorFees
docs: The cumulative child-bounty curator fee for each parent bounty.

storage.name: TotalValueLocked
docs: The sum of funds across all pools.
This might be lower but never higher than the sum of `total_balance` of all [`PoolMembers`]
because calling `pool_withdraw_unbonded` might decrease the total stake of the pool's
`bonded_account` without adjusting the pallet-internal `UnbondingPool`'s.

storage.name: MinJoinBond
docs: Minimum amount to bond to join a pool.

storage.name: MinCreateBond
docs: Minimum bond required to create a pool.
This is the amount that the depositor must put as their initial stake in the pool, as an
indication of "skin in the game".
This is the value that will always exist in the staking ledger of the pool bonded account
while all other accounts leave.

storage.name: MaxPools
docs: Maximum number of nomination pools that can exist. If `None`, then an unbounded number of
pools can exist.

storage.name: MaxPoolMembers
docs: Maximum number of members that can exist in the system. If `None`, then the count
members are not bound on a system wide basis.

storage.name: MaxPoolMembersPerPool
docs: Maximum number of members that may belong to pool. If `None`, then the count of
members is not bound on a per pool basis.

storage.name: GlobalMaxCommission
docs: The maximum commission that can be charged by a pool. Used on commission payouts to bound
pool commissions that are > `GlobalMaxCommission`, necessary if a future
`GlobalMaxCommission` is lower than some current pool commissions.

storage.name: PoolMembers
docs: Active members.
TWOX-NOTE: SAFE since `AccountId` is a secure hash.

storage.name: CounterForPoolMembers
docs: Counter for the related counted storage map

storage.name: BondedPools
docs: Storage for bonded pools.

storage.name: CounterForBondedPools
docs: Counter for the related counted storage map

storage.name: RewardPools
docs: Reward pools. This is where there rewards for each pool accumulate. When a members payout is
claimed, the balance comes out of the reward pool. Keyed by the bonded pools account.

storage.name: CounterForRewardPools
docs: Counter for the related counted storage map

storage.name: SubPoolsStorage
docs: Groups of unbonding pools. Each group of unbonding pools belongs to a
bonded pool, hence the name sub-pools. Keyed by the bonded pools account.

storage.name: CounterForSubPoolsStorage
docs: Counter for the related counted storage map

storage.name: Metadata
docs: Metadata for the pool.

storage.name: CounterForMetadata
docs: Counter for the related counted storage map

storage.name: LastPoolId
docs: Ever increasing number of all pools created so far.

storage.name: ReversePoolIdLookup
docs: A reverse lookup from the pool's account id to its id.
This is only used for slashing and on automatic withdraw update. In all other instances, the
pool id is used, and the accounts are deterministically derived from it.

storage.name: CounterForReversePoolIdLookup
docs: Counter for the related counted storage map

storage.name: ClaimPermissions
docs: Map from a pool member account to their opted claim permission.

storage.name: Pools
docs: Map from `PoolAssetId` to `PoolInfo`. This establishes whether a pool has been officially
created rather than people sending tokens directly to a pool's public account.

storage.name: NextPoolAssetId
docs: Stores the `PoolAssetId` that is going to be used for the next lp token.
This gets incremented whenever a new lp pool is created.

storage.name: PoolFees
docs: Per-pool swap fee overrides.
When a pool has no entry here, the global [`Config::LPFee`] applies. This storage is purely
additive: existing pools and runtimes that never set a per-pool fee behave exactly as before
and require no migration. See [`Pallet::pool_fee`] for the resolution logic.

storage.name: Head
docs: The current "head of the queue" being unstaked.
The head in itself can be a batch of up to [`Config::BatchSize`] stakers.

storage.name: Queue
docs: The map of all accounts wishing to be unstaked.
Keeps track of `AccountId` wishing to unstake and it's corresponding deposit.

storage.name: CounterForQueue
docs: Counter for the related counted storage map

storage.name: ErasToCheckPerBlock
docs: Number of eras to check per block.
If set to 0, this pallet does absolutely nothing. Cannot be set to more than
[`Config::MaxErasToCheckPerBlock`].
Based on the amount of weight available at [`Pallet::on_idle`], up to this many eras are
checked. The checking is represented by updating [`UnstakeRequest::checked`], which is
stored in [`Head`].

storage.name: BookStateFor
docs: The index of the first and last (non-empty) pages.

storage.name: ServiceHead
docs: The origin at which we should begin servicing.

storage.name: Pages
docs: The map of page indices to pages.

storage.name: PausedCalls
docs: The set of calls that are explicitly paused.

storage.name: EnteredUntil
docs: Contains the last block number that the safe-mode will remain entered in.
Set to `None` when safe-mode is exited.
Safe-mode is automatically exited when the current block number exceeds this value.

storage.name: Deposits
docs: Holds the reserve that was taken from an account at a specific block number.
This helps governance to have an overview of outstanding deposits that should be returned or
slashed.

storage.name: Cursor
docs: The currently active migration to run and its cursor.
`None` indicates that no migration is running.

storage.name: Historic
docs: Set of all successfully executed migrations.
This is used as blacklist, to not re-execute migrations that have not been removed from the
codebase yet. Governance can regularly clear this out via `clear_historic`.

storage.name: Configuration
docs: The current configuration of this pallet.

storage.name: Reservations
docs: The Polkadot Core reservations (generally tasked with the maintenance of System Chains).

storage.name: ForceReservations
docs: Force reservations that need to be inserted into the workplan at the next sale rotation.
They are automatically freed at the next sale rotation.

storage.name: Leases
docs: The Polkadot Core legacy leases.

storage.name: Status
docs: The current status of miscellaneous subsystems of this pallet.

storage.name: SaleInfo
docs: The details of the current sale, including its properties and status.

storage.name: PotentialRenewals
docs: Records of potential renewals.
Renewals will only actually be allowed if `CompletionStatus` is actually `Complete`.

storage.name: Regions
docs: The current (unassigned or provisionally assigend) Regions.

storage.name: Workplan
docs: The work we plan on having each core do at a particular time in the future.

storage.name: Workload
docs: The current workload of each core. This gets updated with workplan as timeslices pass.

storage.name: InstaPoolContribution
docs: Record of a single contribution to the Instantaneous Coretime Pool.

storage.name: InstaPoolIo
docs: Record of Coretime entering or leaving the Instantaneous Coretime Pool.

storage.name: InstaPoolHistory
docs: Total InstaPool rewards for each Timeslice and the number of core parts which contributed.

storage.name: CoreCountInbox
docs: Received core count change from the relay chain.

storage.name: AutoRenewals
docs: Keeping track of cores which have auto-renewal enabled.
Sorted by `CoreIndex` to make the removal of cores from auto-renewal more efficient.

storage.name: RevenueInbox
docs: Received revenue info from the relay chain.

storage.name: CurrentSessionIndex
docs: Index of the current session. This may be offset relative to the session index tracked by
eg `pallet_session`; mixnet session indices are independent.

storage.name: CurrentSessionStartBlock
docs: Block in which the current session started.

storage.name: NextAuthorityIds
docs: Authority list for the next session.

storage.name: Mixnodes
docs: Mixnode sets by session index. Only the mixnode sets for the previous, current, and next
sessions are kept; older sets are discarded.
The mixnodes in each set are keyed by authority index so we can easily check if an
authority has registered a mixnode. The authority indices should only be used during
registration; the authority indices for the very first session are made up.

storage.name: Parameters
docs: Stored parameters.

storage.name: PristineCode
docs: A mapping from a contract's code hash to its code.
The code's size is bounded by [`crate::limits::BLOB_BYTES`] for PVM and
[`revm::primitives::eip170::MAX_CODE_SIZE`] for EVM bytecode.

storage.name: CodeInfoOf
docs: A mapping from a contract's code hash to its code info.

storage.name: AccountInfoOf
docs: The data associated to a contract or externally owned account.

storage.name: NativeDepositOf
docs: Native currency storage deposit contributed by a user into a contract.
Bounds how much native value the user can receive back from that contract's
storage deposit.
Keys: `(holder, contributor) -> amount`
- `holder`: account on which the deposit is held (a contract, or the pallet's own account
for code-upload deposits).
- `contributor`: user that funded the deposit. Receives the native portion on refund, capped
at this entry's `amount`.

storage.name: ImmutableDataOf
docs: The immutable data associated with a given account.

storage.name: DeletionQueue
docs: Terminated contracts that await lazy cleanup.
Each entry pairs a child trie ID with the contract account so that `on_idle` can
drain both the child trie and any [`NativeDepositOf`] entries that named the contract
as `holder`. Both can be arbitrarily large, so cleanup runs lazily in `on_idle`.

storage.name: DeletionQueueCounter
docs: A pair of monotonic counters used to track the latest contract marked for deletion
and the latest deleted contract in queue.

storage.name: OriginalAccount
docs: Map a Ethereum address to its original `AccountId32`.
When deriving a `H160` from an `AccountId32` we use a hash function. In order to
reconstruct the original account we need to store the reverse mapping here.
Register your `AccountId32` using [`Pallet::map_account`] in order to
use it with this pallet.

storage.name: EthereumBlock
docs: The current Ethereum block that is stored in the `on_finalize` method.
# Note
This could be further optimized into the future to store only the minimum
information needed to reconstruct the Ethereum block at the RPC level.
Since the block is convenient to have around, and the extra details are capped
by a few hashes and the vector of transaction hashes, we store the block here.

storage.name: BlockHash
docs: Mapping for block number and hashes.
The maximum number of elements stored is capped by the block hash count `BLOCK_HASH_COUNT`.

storage.name: ReceiptInfoData
docs: The details needed to reconstruct the receipt info offchain.
This contains valuable information about the gas used by the transaction.
NOTE: The item is unbound and should therefore never be read on chain.
It could otherwise inflate the PoV size of a block.

storage.name: EthBlockBuilderIR
docs: Incremental ethereum block builder.

storage.name: EthBlockBuilderFirstValues
docs: The first transaction and receipt of the ethereum block.
These values are moved out of the `EthBlockBuilderIR` to avoid serializing and
deserializing them on every transaction. Instead, they are loaded when needed.

storage.name: DebugSettingsOf
docs: Debugging settings that can be configured when DebugEnabled config is true.

storage.name: Delegators
docs: Map of Delegators to their `Delegation`.
Implementation note: We are not using a double map with `delegator` and `agent` account
as keys since we want to restrict delegators to delegate only to one account at a time.

storage.name: CounterForDelegators
docs: Counter for the related counted storage map

storage.name: Agents
docs: Map of `Agent` to their `Ledger`.

storage.name: CounterForAgents
docs: Counter for the related counted storage map

storage.name: Freezes
docs: A map that stores freezes applied on an account for a given AssetId.

storage.name: FrozenBalances
docs: A map that stores the current total frozen balance for every account on a given AssetId.

storage.name: RawValues
docs: The raw values for each oracle operator.
Maps `(AccountId, OracleKey)` to `TimestampedValue` containing the operator's submitted
value along with the timestamp when it was submitted. This storage maintains the complete
history of individual operator submissions, allowing for data aggregation and audit trails.
## Storage Economics
No storage deposits are required as this data is considered essential for the oracle's
operation and data integrity. The storage cost is borne by the blockchain as part of the
oracle infrastructure.

storage.name: Values
docs: The aggregated values for each oracle key.
Maps `OracleKey` to `TimestampedValue`.

storage.name: HasDispatched
docs: A set of accounts that have already fed data in the current block.
This storage item tracks which oracle operators have already submitted data in the
current block to enforce the "one submission per block" rule. This prevents spam and
ensures fair participation among oracle operators.
The storage is cleared at the end of each block in the `on_finalize` hook, resetting
the state for the next block.

storage.name: BountyCount
docs: Number of bounty proposals that have been made.

storage.name: Bounties
docs: Bounties that have been made.

storage.name: ChildBounties
docs: Child bounties that have been added.
Indexed by `(parent_bounty_id, child_bounty_id)`.

storage.name: ChildBountiesPerParent
docs: Number of active child bounties per parent bounty.
Indexed by `parent_bounty_id`.

storage.name: TotalChildBountiesPerParent
docs: Number of total child bounties per parent bounty, including completed bounties.
Indexed by `parent_bounty_id`.

storage.name: ChildBountiesValuePerParent
docs: The cumulative child-bounty value for each parent bounty. To be subtracted from the parent
bounty payout when awarding bounty.
Indexed by `parent_bounty_id`.

storage.name: CuratorDeposit
docs: The consideration cost incurred by the child-/bounty curator for committing to the role.
Determined by [`pallet::Config::Consideration`]. It is created when the curator accepts the
role, and is either burned if the curator misbehaves or consumed upon successful
completion of the child-/bounty.
Note: If the parent curator is also assigned to the child-bounty,
the consideration cost is charged only once — when the curator
accepts the role for the parent bounty.
Indexed by `(parent_bounty_id, child_bounty_id)`.

storage.name: NextAssetIndex
docs: The next available asset index for foreign assets.
This is incremented each time a new foreign asset mapping is created.

storage.name: AssetIndexToForeignAssetId
docs: Mapping an asset index (derived from the precompile address) to a `ForeignAssetId`.

storage.name: ForeignAssetIdToAssetIndex
docs: Mapping a `ForeignAssetId` to an asset index (used for deriving precompile addresses).

storage.name: Nonces
docs: Nonces for permit signatures.
Mapping: (verifying_contract, owner_address) => nonce
Uses Blake2_128Concat for the first key to prevent storage collision attacks
when the verifying_contract address could be influenced by an attacker.
Note: EIP-2612 specifies uint256 nonce. We store as U256 for compatibility.

storage.name: NextFreeParaId
docs: The next para id that [`Pallet::reserve`] will hand out.

storage.name: NextMessageId
docs: The id the next message to the relay chain will carry.
One per message sent, echoed back in the relay chain's response, so a request, its
response and the events on both chains can be tied together.

storage.name: Paras
docs: Every para id reserved through this pallet, and what is happening with it.

storage.name: PendingRegistrations
docs: Registrations waiting on their validation code, by para id.
Counted so [`Config::MaxPendingRegistrations`] can be enforced with a single read.

storage.name: CounterForPendingRegistrations
docs: Counter for the related counted storage map
